sections.h2: Which court handles an Arkansas probate?
sections.html:
File in the circuit court of the county where the deceased lived. Under Ark. Code 28-40-102, a nonresident's estate goes to the county holding most of the in-state property by value, and a person who died in Arkansas with no home or property here is handled where the death occurred.

Arkansas has 75 counties, so the clerk you deal with depends on where the owner lived and where the house sits. When cases start in two counties, the later one waits until the circuit court in the first county decides venue. A judge may also move a case before final distribution if it was filed in the wrong county or a transfer helps the estate.

A house in Garland County can belong to an estate opened in Pulaski County. The recorder in the county where the land lies still records the deeds. Probate court and recorder are separate offices, so expect to visit or mail both.

First in line is the executor named in the will, then the surviving spouse, then other people who share in the estate. Section 28-48-101 sets that order and attaches short deadlines.

  • A surviving spouse, or the spouse's nominee, petitions within 30 days after the death.
  • Other people entitled to a share, or their nominee, apply within 40 days if there is a spouse and within 30 days if there is none.
  • Any other qualified person may apply after those windows.

Disqualified: anyone under 18, a person of unsound mind, an unpardoned felon, a corporation not authorized to act as a fiduciary in Arkansas, and anyone the court finds unsuitable. A nonresident can serve only if an agent is appointed to accept papers, and the court clerk may be that agent. Heirs who live out of state should sort this out before they plan to serve.

sections.h2: Who owns the house at the moment of death?
sections.html:
With no will, real estate passes to the heirs at once, while personal property goes to the personal representative. Ark. Code 28-9-203 sets that rule and 28-9-206 limits it.

The limits are the surviving spouse's dower or curtesy, homestead rights of the spouse and children, and statutory allowances for a spouse and minor children. A spouse married to the decedent for more than a year can also elect against a will. When there are no descendants the spouse takes the estate, and a marriage of under three years cuts the spouse's share to 50%.

An heir can therefore hold title on paper and still be unable to deliver a clean sale. Buyers, title companies and lenders want to know who the heirs are and whether the court has appointed anyone. Homestead rights of a spouse or child can shrink what an heir is free to sell.

sections.h2: Small estates without a formal case
sections.html:
A distributee, meaning an heir, may collect a small estate by affidavit when no petition for a personal representative is pending, 45 days have gone by, and the net estate is $100,000 or less. The homestead and the spousal and child allowances are left out of that count. The terms are in Ark. Code 28-41-101.

File the affidavit with the probate clerk in the proper county. It gives a legal description and value for any real property, names who lives there, and lists the people entitled to receive it. It also states that no claims are unpaid and that any Department of Human Services benefits were reimbursed. Filing costs $25, each certified copy costs $5, and attaching a will adds nothing.

When real estate is involved, the distributee publishes notice of the death and the filing within 30 days. Creditors then have three months from first publication to present verified claims. Before you rely on an affidavit to sell land, ask the title company whether it will accept that document to move title.

In a formal administration, creditors generally get six months from the first published notice, and Section 28-50-101 bars late claims, with a few timing rules layered on top.

EventTime period
Standard claim deadline6 months after first publication
Copy of notice to known heirs and creditorsWithin 1 month after first publication
Extra time if a creditor is served late30 more days after the period ends
Known creditors who never got noticeBarred 2 years after first publication
Outer limit if no letters or notice5 years after death
Small estate affidavit, real property3 months from first publication

Mortgages and other liens on estate property sit outside the claims deadline. A lender with a mortgage on the house keeps its lien after the six months run, so the payoff comes out of any sale.

When a personal representative sells land, the court order sets the terms and an appraisal comes first. See 28-51-302 and 28-51-303.

  • Three disinterested appraisers who know local values appraise the property under oath. The court may approve a single appraiser if no heir or beneficiary objects.
  • The appraisal is filed with the clerk before the court issues the sale order.
  • The order says whether the sale is private or by auction, and whether it is for cash or on payment terms.
  • A private sale must bring at least the full appraised value. An auction must bring at least three-fourths of it.
  • A sale cannot close more than six months after the order unless a court-ordered reappraisal happened within the 30 days before the sale.

Those floors mean every offer on a probate house gets measured against the appraisal and the hearing schedule, including an as-is cash offer.

sections.h2: How long a will can wait
sections.html:
An application to probate a will must come within five years of the death under Ark. Code 28-40-103. Exceptions cover fraudulent concealment of a will and a nonresident's will already probated elsewhere.

A late probate of a nonresident's will does not harm a buyer who recorded a purchase of Arkansas real property from that estate. Families who leave a house sitting for years should know the clock exists. Waiting also lets taxes, insurance and repair bills pile up on a property nobody has authority over.

Typical problems are unclear authority, heirs in several states, a mortgage still in the decedent's name, and a house left empty. Each slows a sale differently.

  • No one has been appointed, so no one can sign for the estate.
  • Heirs disagree about keeping or selling, and all of them hold an interest in real estate that passes at death.
  • Property taxes keep coming, and the tax lien ranks ahead of other liens, so unpaid bills follow the house.
  • A court-approved sale must meet the appraisal floor and wait for a hearing date.

Cash Home Buyers makes as-is offers on inherited houses in Arkansas. Bring the court paperwork you have, and ask an Arkansas probate attorney which route fits your estate.

faqs.q: Do all Arkansas estates have to go through probate?
faqs.a: No. When no petition for a personal representative is pending, 45 days have gone by and the net estate is $100,000 or less (not counting the homestead and family allowances), a distributee can use the small estate affidavit. Larger estates, and estates where authority is disputed, go through the circuit court.

faqs.q: How soon must a spouse ask to be named personal representative?
faqs.a: Within 30 days after the death, if the spouse wants priority over other heirs. Other people entitled to a share apply within 40 days when there is a surviving spouse and within 30 days when there is none, under Ark. Code 28-48-101.

faqs.q: Can heirs sell the house before the estate is closed?
faqs.a: With no will, real estate passes to the heirs at death, but spouse and child homestead rights still apply. Buyers and title companies usually want proof of who has authority, so most sales wait for an appointment or an accepted affidavit.

faqs.q: What price must a probate house bring?
faqs.a: A court-ordered private sale must reach at least the full appraised value, and an auction at least three-fourths of it. The sale cannot close later than six months after the order without a fresh court-ordered appraisal.

faqs.q: Does a mortgage disappear when the owner dies?
faqs.a: No. The claims deadline leaves mortgages and other liens on estate property alone, so the lender keeps its lien and the balance is paid from sale proceeds.
